damvi+damvi.headline: Double the warmth, double the dawats, half the rest.
damvi+damvi.dynamic: Two Damvi spouses are the couple everyone wants at the family function: warm, chatty, generous and always laughing. In Unani terms you share the same warm, moist qualities, so you understand each other's need for people, variety and celebration without any explanation. That shared sunshine is a real strength in a marriage. The catch is that identical qualities tend to amplify. Nobody naturally plays the grounding, cooling role, so overspending, overeating, overcommitting and late nights can quietly become the household norm. Big decisions may be made in a burst of excitement and regretted later. The healthiest Damvi homes deliberately borrow a little coolness and dryness: planning, budgeting and quiet time.
damvi+damvi.home_life: Expect a busy kitchen and a full dastarkhwan, so agree early to keep weekday food simple: daal, sabzi and salad, with rich dishes saved for weekends. You both run warm, so AC fights are rare, though the electricity bill may not be. Sleep schedules can slide later as guests linger past midnight. Set a household lights-out time and protect it, even in shaadi season.
tips: Make one of you the household 'finance minister' each month, then switch roles.
Follow every big family event with a light-food week at home.
Keep two evenings a week completely free of guests and outings.
Before any big decision, sleep on it for at least one night.

damvi+safravi.headline: Warm hearts, quick sparks, and plenty getting done.
damvi+safravi.dynamic: This pairing shares heat: both of you are energetic, expressive and quick to act, and life together rarely feels dull. Damvi's moisture brings softness and flexibility, which cushions Safravi's sharp, dry intensity, while Safravi brings the focus and follow-through Damvi sometimes lacks. In Unani terms, you balance each other on the moist-dry axis but double up on warmth. That means arguments can flare fast, especially in summer, when either of you is hungry, or after a long day. The good news is that both of you also cool down quickly and rarely sulk. Learn to pause before reacting, and this becomes a lively, productive partnership.
damvi+safravi.home_life: Food can be a happy meeting point, but watch the spice and the richness: Safravi wants it fiery, Damvi wants it buttery, and neither of you needs both. Keep raita and salad on every table. Room temperature fights are mild because you both run warm, so the AC stays on. Sleep may differ: Damvi drops off easily while Safravi lies awake thinking, so agree on quiet, dim evenings.
tips: Agree on a 20-minute cool-off rule before continuing any argument.
Discuss serious matters after meals, never on an empty stomach.
Let Safravi lead the plans and Damvi lead the people, and credit each other.
Cook one cooling meal together each day through the summer months.

damvi+balghami.headline: Warm sunshine meets still water: an easy, loving balance.
damvi+balghami.dynamic: This is one of the most comfortable pairings. You share moisture, which in Unani terms brings softness, flexibility and an easy emotional flow, while Damvi's warmth balances Balghami's coolness. Damvi brings energy, laughter and a social life; Balghami brings patience, calm and steadiness. Arguments are rare and usually mild. The main difference is pace. Damvi wants to say yes to every dawat and plan; Balghami would rather spend a quiet evening at home. Left unspoken, Damvi may feel held back and Balghami may feel dragged along. Respect both rhythms and you'll have a home that is both lively and restful, which is rarer than it sounds.
damvi+balghami.home_life: You both enjoy food, so the shared risk is heavy, rich meals and late dinners. Keep dinners light and early, and add a family walk afterwards. Room temperature can be a gentle tug-of-war: Damvi runs warm and wants the fan on, Balghami feels the cold and reaches for a blanket. Sleep comes easily to both, but Balghami needs more, so let them have the slower Sunday mornings.
tips: Agree on a weekly rhythm: one social outing, one quiet night in.
Balghami: say what you want early instead of simply going along.
Damvi: check with your spouse before committing the family to plans.
Walk together after dinner; it suits both of your temperaments.

damvi+saudavi.headline: Perfect opposites: lightness meets depth, and both grow.
damvi+saudavi.dynamic: Unani tradition sees opposite qualities as the heart of balance, and these two temperaments are opposite on both axes: warm-moist meets cool-dry. Damvi brings cheer, ease and sociability; Saudavi brings depth, planning and loyalty. Damvi lifts Saudavi out of worry, and Saudavi helps Damvi slow down and finish things. The challenge is translation. Damvi may read Saudavi's silence as rejection, and Saudavi may read Damvi's cheerfulness as not taking life seriously. Neither is true. When both learn to see the other as a balancing force rather than a problem to fix, this pairing can become one of the most complementary marriages in the whole Mizaj system.
damvi+saudavi.home_life: Food needs differ in a useful way: Damvi does best on lighter, cooler meals and Saudavi on warm, moist, nourishing ones, so a dastarkhwan with both yakhni and salad keeps everyone happy. Room temperature is the classic fight: Damvi throws off the blanket while Saudavi wraps up in a shawl, so use separate quilts. Sleep differs too, since Damvi sleeps deeply and Saudavi lightly, so keep the bedroom calm and dark.
tips: Damvi: ask about feelings gently instead of filling silences with jokes.
Saudavi: celebrate small wins with your spouse instead of analysing them.
Plan finances together: Saudavi drafts the budget, Damvi keeps it human.
Keep one shared ritual, like Friday evening chai, just for the two of you.

safravi+safravi.headline: Two flames: brilliant together, but someone must cool the room.
safravi+safravi.dynamic: Two Safravi spouses understand each other's ambition, speed and high standards instantly. You can build a career, a business or a household at remarkable pace, and neither of you will tolerate laziness. But in Unani terms, identical warm, dry qualities amplify, and nobody naturally cools the fire. Arguments can escalate quickly, both of you want to be right, and pride can turn a small disagreement into a week-long cold war. Competition may creep in: over careers, over who handles family matters better, even over who is more tired. This pairing works best when both partners consciously take turns stepping back, and treat rest, softness and appreciation as household duties.
safravi+safravi.home_life: Spicy, oily food will become the default unless you choose otherwise, so build cooling meals into the week: lauki, daal, raita and lassi. Room temperature fights are rare; you both want the AC on and the room cold. Sleep is the weak spot, with two busy minds still running at midnight. Agree on a screen-free wind-down, and never discuss work or family problems in bed.
tips: Name a 'cooler' for each argument, and take turns in that role.
Divide responsibilities clearly so you are partners, not competitors.
Never decide anything important when either of you is hungry or overheated.
Say one specific appreciation out loud every single day.

safravi+balghami.headline: Fire meets water: a classic Unani balance.
safravi+balghami.dynamic: In Unani terms this is a textbook balance: warm-dry Safravi and cool-moist Balghami are opposite on both qualities. Safravi brings drive, decisions and energy; Balghami brings patience, calm and emotional steadiness. Balghami's presence can cool Safravi's temper the way water settles a flame, and Safravi's urgency can get Balghami moving on plans that would otherwise wait for years. The friction is pace. Safravi may feel Balghami is too slow; Balghami may feel steamrolled and rushed. If Safravi learns to wait and Balghami learns to speak up early instead of retreating into silence, this pairing becomes calm, productive and deeply secure.
safravi+balghami.home_life: Food preferences pull in opposite directions: Safravi wants cooling dishes and Balghami wants warm, spiced ones. A dastarkhwan with both raita and a ginger-rich yakhni solves it. The AC remote is the real battlefield: Safravi wants it at 22 while Balghami reaches for a shawl, so compromise on a fan plus a light blanket. Balghami sleeps early and deeply; Safravi stays up, so keep late-night screens out of the bedroom.
tips: Safravi: give a decision a day before pushing for an answer.
Balghami: share your view early, before resentment has time to build.
Split tasks by strength: Safravi starts things, Balghami sees them through.
Keep a fan-and-blanket compromise ready for summer nights.

safravi+saudavi.headline: Sharp minds, high standards, and a need for softness.
safravi+saudavi.dynamic: These two share dryness, which in Unani terms brings precision, structure and seriousness. Both value logic, competence and doing things properly, and you will respect each other's minds. Saudavi's coolness can temper Safravi's heat, and Safravi's energy can push Saudavi's careful plans into action. The risk is that neither temperament brings much moisture: softness, flexibility, easy affection. Criticism can become the household language, and both of you may keep score. Safravi may find Saudavi too cautious and gloomy; Saudavi may find Safravi too hasty and harsh. With deliberate warmth, compliments and forgiveness, this can be a powerful, respectful partnership that gets a great deal done.
safravi+saudavi.home_life: Both of you are traditionally prone to dryness, so meals with moisture help the whole house: dahi, lauki, soups, milk and fresh fruit. Room temperature is a real divide: Safravi runs hot and Saudavi runs cold, so expect the AC-versus-shawl debate most nights. Sleep is light for both, one from a racing mind and one from a worrying one, so a calm, dark, screen-free bedroom matters doubly here.
tips: Replace one criticism a day with one specific appreciation.
Let Saudavi research, then let Safravi decide by an agreed deadline.
Add moist, nourishing dishes to the weekly menu for both of you.
Set aside time to talk about feelings, not only logistics.

balghami+balghami.headline: A peaceful home that needs a gentle push forward.
balghami+balghami.dynamic: Two Balghami spouses create one of the gentlest homes imaginable: patient, kind, rarely a raised voice, plenty of forgiveness. You both value family, stability and comfort, and you understand each other's need for rest. But in Unani terms, identical cool, moist qualities amplify, and nobody naturally brings the warmth and movement that gets things going. Decisions about money, careers, moving house or even fixing the leaking tap can drift for months. Both of you may avoid difficult conversations to keep the peace, letting small issues grow quietly. This pairing thrives when you build structure into the relationship: planning days, shared goals and taking turns as the motivator.
balghami+balghami.home_life: Comfort food is your shared love language, so watch for heavy, creamy, late dinners becoming routine. Add warming spices, eat earlier and take an evening walk together. Room temperature rarely causes fights, since you both prefer warmth, so heaters and quilts will be popular. Sleep is deep for both of you, which is lovely until nobody gets up for Fajr. Set one alarm and agree who gets out of bed first.
tips: Hold a short monthly 'planning chai' to settle pending decisions.
Take turns being the one who says 'let's do it now'.
Exercise together; it is far easier to keep going as a pair.
Raise small concerns early, before peace turns into silence.

balghami+saudavi.headline: Quiet, loyal and steady: a calm home that needs warmth.
balghami+saudavi.dynamic: You share coolness, which in Unani terms brings calm, reflection and a preference for quiet over drama. Balghami's moisture softens Saudavi's dryness: their easygoing patience helps soothe Saudavi's worries and perfectionism. Saudavi, in turn, brings planning and direction to Balghami's relaxed approach. This can be a deeply loyal, low-conflict marriage. The risk is coldness in the emotional sense. Neither temperament naturally initiates outings, celebrations or open expressions of feeling, so the home can grow too still and both partners can withdraw at the same time. Adding warmth deliberately, through company, shared activities and spoken affection, is what makes this pairing flourish.
balghami+saudavi.home_life: You will both crave warm food, so the kitchen will lean towards yakhni, chai and comfort dishes; just keep them freshly cooked and not too heavy. Room temperature fights are rare, since you both feel the cold: expect heaters, quilts and shared shawls. Sleep schedules differ, with Balghami sleeping long and deep and Saudavi lightly and later, so keep the bedroom quiet and allow different wake-up times.
tips: Plan one social outing or dawat every week, and keep the promise.
Ask 'how are you really?' and wait for the full answer.
Saudavi: share plans early. Balghami: share feelings early.
Get morning sunlight together at weekends, even on a short walk.

saudavi+saudavi.headline: Deep, loyal and serious: bring the sunshine in on purpose.
saudavi+saudavi.dynamic: Two Saudavi spouses understand each other at a level few couples reach. You share a love of order, careful thought, privacy and loyalty, and you will rarely be careless with each other's trust. But in Unani terms, identical cool, dry qualities amplify. Worry can echo between you, and both of you may sink into the same low mood at the same time, especially in winter. Criticism, perfectionism and long silences can take the place of open conversation. The strongest Saudavi homes deliberately import warmth and moisture: cheerful company, shared laughter, nourishing food, and partners who take turns being the optimist when the other is low.
saudavi+saudavi.home_life: Warm, moist, nourishing food helps both of you: soups, a little ghee, milk, eggs and soaked dry fruit. Don't let the household run on chai and rusks. Room temperature is easy, since you will both want it warm. Sleep is the shared weak spot: two light sleepers with two busy minds. Keep a fixed bedtime, put the phones away, and leave the day's worries in a notebook rather than on the pillow.
tips: Take turns being the optimist when one of you is low.
Invite cheerful friends or cousins over regularly.
Choose one fun, completely unproductive activity together each week.
Agree on a weekly 'worry time' so it doesn't leak into every evening.
